Design fire transcribed as a linear ramp 0 -> 300 kW over 0-30 s, then constant to 600 s (hrr_curve). growth='ultrafast' and time_to_peak_s=30 are also set; hrr_curve takes precedence.
Fire surface is the top face of the burner block at z = 0.2 m: 0.5 x 0.4 = 0.2 m2, so HRRPUA = 1500 kW/m2.
Fuel is methane (CH4: C=1, H=4, O=0, N=0) with heat of combustion 50 000 kJ/kg, CO yield 0 and a nominal soot yield of 0.001 (the schema requires a value above 0).
Burner and inlet-duct obstructions use INERT surfaces. The official steel, aluminium-silicate and Marinite linings are not modelled.

The passive inlet duct is a permanent OPEN vent on the y = 0 wall (x 0.7-1.0, z 0.6-0.9). The HVAC duct losses from the official input are not modelled. This vent sits against the end of the horizontal duct obstruction, so its effective flow should be checked.
The EXHAUST vent, the drop ceiling and the door are not modelled. The door stays closed and envelope leakage is ignored, as requested.
Uniform mesh of 0.15 m (40 x 27 x 30 cells), simulated from 0 to 600 s with no pre-ignition period (official T_BEGIN = -60 s ignored).
Ambient conditions are left at FDS defaults (official TMPA = 21 C and P_INF = 99 300 Pa are not carried over).
Device output every 1 s and slice output every 5 s (defaults).
The evacuation path ends at the door location at (4.8 ; 0.3 ; 1.8) even though the door is closed in this test. RSET = 120 s.
